sections.html:
West-central Alabama holds Tuscaloosa County, which stretches across 1,351 square miles. Wooded hills yield to flatter coastal plain as you head south. The Black Warrior River runs through it, and Lake Tuscaloosa spreads over about 5,000 acres. Part of the Talladega National Forest lies inside the line. Houses near water, hills or the forest edge each carry their own access, flood and insurance questions.

The city of Tuscaloosa is both seat and biggest city, with Northport and Brookwood rounding out the three. Towns include Coaling, Coker, Lake View, Moundville, Vance and Woodstock.

Population reached 227,036 in 2020, a jump of 16.6 percent over 194,656 in 2010, and is estimated at 241,368 for 2025. There are 101,460 housing units and 89,962 households, and 11.3 percent of the units sat empty. Owners occupy 58.9 percent of occupied homes while 41.1 percent are rented. Landlords should note the 11.6 percent rental vacancy rate: a house with a difficult tenant history or lease damage can wait a good while for the next renter.

The median age is 32.9, partly because the University of Alabama, Shelton State and Stillman College keep a steady stream of students in the rental market. Roughly 68.9 percent of residents live in urban areas and 31.1 percent in rural ones.

Two public systems share the county. Tuscaloosa City Schools serves the city, with Paul W. Bryant, Central and Northridge high schools, and the Tuscaloosa County School System serves everyone outside it. Confirm which one covers your address before you promise a buyer a school zone in the listing. The two systems each run their own set of campuses, and a house just inside or outside the city line may belong to the other.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax and when it is due
sections.html:
County offices at 714 Greensboro Ave in Tuscaloosa handle the tax. The Tax Assessor sets values and the Tax Collector bills and collects. The collector is in Room 124 at (205) 464-8230, open Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5pm, except holidays. The assessor is in Room 108 at (205) 464-8240.

DateWhat happens
October 1Property taxes are due
November 15Mortgage company escrow payments due; notices go to those companies electronically, not by mail
December 31Last day to pay without penalty or interest; a postmark of that day is accepted
January 1Taxes delinquent, penalties added, delinquent notices sent
March 15Personal checks no longer accepted after this date; pay by cash or money order
End of MarchLast week to pay before tax lien fees are added
AprilImpending tax sale advertised online
Last week of AprilAnnual tax sale, held online only

An out-of-date mailing address is how people miss a bill. After a sale, give the collector a forwarding address for anything that comes later.

sections.h2: How the county values a house
sections.html:
Alabama law requires the appraisal department to keep real estate values current on a four-year cycle, and appraisers check yearly changes too. Reasons a value gets reviewed include a building permit, a septic permit, a recent sale or a request from the owner. The assessor's page offers a protest form, a homestead type chart, income qualifications, a millage chart and a form for disability requirements.

Because permits can set off a review, a permitted remodel may bring a new valuation, so weigh that before putting money into a house you plan to sell. Ask the assessor's office whether the work you have in mind is likely to change the record.

Send a written protest to the County Board of Equalization. Alabama gives you 30 days after the written notice of valuation, and the Code of Alabama sections 40-3-20, 40-3-24 and 40-3-25 govern the process. Use the deadline printed on your own notice, and get the protest form from the assessor's page or office.

Severe weather is part of life here, and an EF4 tornado struck Tuscaloosa on April 27, 2011. Where your house had storm repairs, hold on to permits and receipts. Buyers and lenders sometimes ask for dated proof of roof, siding or structural work, and a missing record can slow a sale.

Delinquency does not bar a sale. Your closing agent requests a payoff from the Tax Collector, and the amount comes out of your proceeds. Ask early, well before any April tax sale notice could cloud the deal. A late payer cannot use a personal check once March 15 passes.

Bring the deed, photo ID and your latest statement to the closing. If you inherited the house, expect to show who has the authority to sign.

Mortgage escrow accounts are paid by the lender, and notices for them go out electronically around mid-November. If you pay your own tax, treat the last days of December as a hard stop and send payment early. A postmark of the final day is accepted, but waiting adds risk for no gain.

Once January arrives, penalties are added and delinquent notices go out. The end of March is the last stretch before tax lien fees apply. A seller who is behind should aim to pay or to close before that point, because lien fees raise the payoff and the April sale notice can make buyers and lenders nervous.

Round up the deed, your latest tax statement, any protest correspondence, permits and receipts for storm or remodel work, and the names of every person on the title. A rental owner should add leases and a note of any damage claims. Heirs should bring the death certificate and any court documents. A tidy file helps the title company, answers the questions a buyer's lender will ask, and shortens the time between acceptance and closing.

With a median age of 32.9 and 41.1 percent of occupied homes rented, a former rental can carry wear that a family buyer may not accept.

  • Student rentals with deferred repairs after turnover.
  • Storm-damaged roofs and trees in a county with a recent tornado history.
  • Estate houses where heirs live outside the county.
  • Property bills that went to an old mailing address.

A cash sale can close without a lender's repair demands, and the tax balance is settled from the proceeds at closing. The University of Alabama is the largest employer and the Mercedes-Benz plant near Vance is the main industrial anchor, so local demand is steady, but sellers still face the issues above.

sections.h2: How a sale moves from offer to closing
sections.html: After you accept an offer, the title company searches the record, orders the tax payoff and schedules the signing. You sign the deed, the county is paid from the proceeds and the rest comes to you. A cash buyer removes the lender appraisal, which often speeds the timeline when a house needs repairs.

faqs.q: When are Tuscaloosa County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1. December 31 is the last day to pay without penalties or interest, and taxes turn delinquent on January 1.

faqs.q: Where is the Tuscaloosa County Tax Collector?
faqs.a: At 714 Greensboro Ave, Room 124, Tuscaloosa, AL 35401, phone (205) 464-8230. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5pm, except holidays.

faqs.q: When does the Tuscaloosa County tax sale happen?
faqs.a: The county advertises it online in April and holds the annual sale, online only, in the last week of April.

faqs.q: How often does Tuscaloosa County reappraise property?
faqs.a: Alabama law requires real estate values to be reestablished within a four-year period, and appraisers review yearly changes as well.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Tuscaloosa County house with delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing agent gets a payoff from the Tax Collector, and the balance is paid from the sale proceeds.
